title: When the Detention Burns
premise: Rafael Underhill, a seventeen-year-old coder who hides behind an anonymous account that keeps exposing the school's secrets, has spent his life being invisible — until the ghost of Marisol Vega, a student who died in the 1970s auditorium fire, begins leaving him notes in ink that shouldn't exist. Her messages lead him to evidence that the school board covered up the fire's true cause to protect a founding family's legacy, and that Marisol's death was no accident. As Rafael falls for Theo, the board chair's son who is auditioning for the lead role in the anniversary production, he must choose between staying safe and burning the whole inheritance down. In the end, Rafael exposes the buried truth during the final audition itself, freeing Marisol's spirit and claiming — for the first time — a name and a love of his own.
about_author: Ulyana Montrose is the pen name of a former boarding-school archivist who spent years cataloguing letters no one was meant to read. She writes young adult gothic mysteries about quiet kids who refuse to stay quiet.

chapters.title: The Account Nobody Owns
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Rafael posts anonymously about the school's rotting auditorium, careful as always, then deletes everything twice before bed. We see his rituals of invisibility and his loneliness. Emotional beat: the ache of being safe and unseen.

chapters.title: Ink That Wasn't There
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. A note appears inside his locker addressed 'Rafael Underhill' — his full name, which no one uses — written in ink that shifts color and dries cold. He tells himself it's a prank. Emotional beat: first crack in his armor of anonymity.

chapters.title: Marisol Vega, 1974
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Researching the school's legendary ghost, he finds Marisol's photo: a girl erased from every yearbook except one smudged page. The notes continue, now quoting things only Rafael has typed. Emotional beat: dread braided with fascination.

chapters.title: Theo Ashcombe Auditions
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Theo, the board chair's golden son, lands the lead in the anniversary production and asks Rafael — the quiet coder — to run the show's projections. Their hands touch over a lighting console. Emotional beat: unwanted warmth.

chapters.title: What the Board Buried
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Following Marisol's clues into the archive basement, Rafael finds a sealed incident report contradicting the official fire story: the blaze started in the founders' private box, not backstage. Emotional beat: the thrill and terror of knowing too much.

chapters.title: A Name Is a Door
chapters.summary: POV Marisol (interlude). The ghost remembers dying and remembers being silenced; naming Rafael was her first act of will in fifty years. She watches him read her notes. Emotional beat: grief sharpened into purpose.

chapters.title: Rehearsal, Interrupted
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. During rehearsal, the ghost lights flare and the sprinklers trigger on a cloudless night; the director blames faulty wiring, but Rafael sees wet footprints leading to the founders' box. Emotional beat: the past refusing to stay past.

chapters.title: Theo's Inheritance
chapters.summary: POV Theo. Theo confesses over stolen rooftop cigarettes that his family's name is on the school's founding plaque — and that his father expects him to defend it blindly. He likes Rafael precisely because Rafael doesn't care about any of it. Emotional beat: two boys comparing cages.

chapters.title: The Second Report
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Marisol leads him to a hidden second document: a witness statement from a janitor who saw someone lock the auditorium doors that night. The signature belongs to Theo's great-grandfather. Emotional beat: the personal cost of truth.

chapters.title: Someone Is Watching
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Rafael notices a security consultant photographing students near the archive; his anonymous account is flagged and nearly traced. He wipes his drives and stops answering Marisol's notes out of fear. Emotional beat: old survival instincts closing like a fist.

chapters.title: Cold Ink, Warm Hands
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Theo finds Rafael shaking in the projection booth after the trace attempt and stays, saying nothing, until morning. Rafael almost tells him everything. Emotional beat: intimacy as both refuge and risk.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Gala
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. At the gala celebrating the school's history, the board unveils a sanitized memorial to 'the tragedy of 1974.' Marisol's rage cracks the chandeliers; only Rafael sees. Emotional beat: fury at beautiful lies.

chapters.title: Locked Doors Again
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Rafael is trapped overnight in the auditorium — doors locked exactly as they were in 1974 — while the consultant searches his locker. Marisol walks him through her last night alive, step by step. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into witness.

chapters.title: She Was Going to Sing
chapters.summary: POV Marisol (interlude). Marisol relives the final audition she never got to finish, and the founder's son who locked the doors because her voice threatened his family's secret. Emotional beat: stolen future, unbroken voice.

chapters.title: Telling Theo
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Rafael shows Theo the documents. Theo's world tilts: his inheritance is a crime scene. His father dismisses the evidence as forgery and threatens expulsion. Emotional beat: love tested by blood loyalty.

chapters.title: The Consultant's File
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Rafael turns his coding skills outward, hacking the consultant's cloud and discovering the board hired him weeks ago — they've known someone was digging since Rafael's very first post. Emotional beat: the hunter realizing he was always the quarry.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: POV Theo. Theo chooses: he copies his family's private letters — proof of the cover-up — and gives them to Rafael, knowing it ends his name, his allowance, his father. Emotional beat: inheritance refused.

chapters.title: Dress Rehearsal Sabotage
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. The board moves to cancel the production and seal the auditorium permanently. Marisol's power surges dangerously; Rafael realizes if the truth doesn't come out at the final audition, it never will — and she may take the building down with everyone in it. Emotional beat: the clock running out.

chapters.title: Final Audition
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. During the final audition, Rafael hijacks the projection system and broadcasts the documents, the janitor's statement, and Marisol's name to the packed house while Theo sings the song she never finished. Emotional beat: climax — visibility chosen at last.

chapters.title: Ashes Answer
chapters.summary: POV Rafael and Marisol. The board collapses under public outrage; the consultant's files leak. In the emptied auditorium, Marisol's ink turns warm for the first time, and she writes not a demand but a goodbye. Emotional beat: release.

chapters.title: The Underhill Byline
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Rafael publishes the full investigation under his real name, byline and all, and faces the fallout — suspension hearings, reporters, his mother's fear — without flinching. Emotional beat: the cost of a name, gladly paid.

chapters.title: Encore
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Months later, the restored auditorium reopens with a plaque bearing Marisol Vega's name. Theo takes Rafael's hand in the front row as the house lights dim. On Rafael's palm, faint and fading, one last note in impossible ink: thank you. Emotional beat: love against duty, memory inherited forward.
